insider_note: Write the equation exactly, coefficients and all. Sixteen ATP is the number examiners check.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The equation
steps.margin_note: Two lines, both coefficients correct. Nothing else is needed for this mark.
steps.why: The equation is the whole answer, so the coefficients are the content rather than decoration.
common_mistakes: Writing NH3 without the coefficient 2. One N2 gives TWO ammonia molecules.
Leaving out the 16 ATP. The energy cost is the point of the equation.
steps.memory_tip: Sixteen ATP for one nitrogen molecule: the most expensive reaction in the plant.

steps.label: What it shows
steps.margin_note: Name the enzyme, the product and why the ATP cost is high.

lines.text: Sixteen ATP to break one N triple bond

lines: Nitrogen fixation converts atmospheric N2 into
The 16 ATP show how much energy it costs to
break the triple bond in N2.
steps.why: The N triple bond is one of the strongest in nature, which is why the reaction needs so much ATP and why only a few organisms can do it.
common_mistakes: Naming no enzyme. Nitrogenase carries out the reaction.
Saying nitrogen is converted to nitrate here. The product of FIXATION is ammonia.
steps.memory_tip: A triple bond is expensive to break, and the ATP count says how expensive.
